extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners and patent office staff (Australian patent administration)
extracted.subtask_description: An official electronic Manual of Practice and Procedure that sets out the legal standards, procedures and authorised practices for searching, examination, oppositions, amendments and other patent-office actions for national and international patent applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of the Manual (accuracy and accessibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide accurate and consistent content that is readily accessible and in a format that enables users to readily apply the relevant information; distinguish practices and procedures from educational information about the Patents Act and case law; ensure all information relevant to patent law and practice is discoverable and accessible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Manual is a controlled document published exclusively electronically and its accuracy can only be guaranteed when viewed electronically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards and expectations for the quality of work and decisions produced by examiners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See chapter 3 for quality-related guidance and the role of peer review and quality checklists (e.g. Annex U/Annex H for ISRs/IPE quality).

rubrics_metrics.name: Customer Service Charter (Timeliness Guidelines)
rubrics_metrics.description: Timeliness expectations and customer service standards the office aims to meet in processing applications and interacting with applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes timeliness targets and guidelines for communications with applicants and third parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Efficient Examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles and practices intended to make examination processes efficient while meeting legal standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers use of tools and procedures to avoid unnecessary work and ensure timely processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of FERs (Earlier Search and Examination Reports)
rubrics_metrics.description: How and when examiners should use earlier search and examination reports to inform current searching and examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes procedural guidance on integrating FERs into the examiner's search and opinion.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Approach to Examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Overarching approach examiners should take when examining applications nationally and internationally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes guidance on restricting searches, reserving opinion, and the appropriate level of detail in reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Level of Detail in the Report
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on how detailed an examiner's report should be when explaining findings and objections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balances the need to explain reasoning with efficiency and consistency across sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reserving Opinion and Restricting the Search
rubrics_metrics.description: Circumstances and approach for limiting the scope of search or reserving an opinion when full searching is impractical or unnecessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes criteria for when to restrict searching and how to record reserved opinions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communicating with the Applicant and Third Parties
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards and allowable practices for examiner communications with applicants, agents and third parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers informal communications, procedural notifications, and limits on providing advice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assisting Unrepresented Applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on how examiners may assist applicants who do not have representation, while maintaining impartiality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains permissible assistance and boundaries to avoid giving unfair advantage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staff Delegations, and Restrictions on Providing Customer Assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: Delegation of powers and limits on examiners' ability to provide advice or act for applicants, including conflict of interest rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers Commissioner's power to make delegations, conflict of interest, and types of delegations and restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search Theory — Objectives of the Search
rubrics_metrics.description: The goals searchers/examiners must keep in mind when conducting a prior art search (e.g., novelty, inventive step assessments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also addresses iterative searching and stopping criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search Theory — Iterative Searching
rubrics_metrics.description: Approach of progressively refining search strategy based on findings and claim construction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasises adapting search areas and keywords as the inventive concept is clarified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Classification Systems (IPC, CPC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use and structure of patent classification systems (International Patent Classification, Cooperative Patent Classification) in searching and indexing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes structure, headings, notes, indexing codes, C-sets, and practice for revisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles of Classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for allocating classification symbols to documents (invention information vs additional information, priority rules, function/application-oriented places).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers first/last place priority rules, common rule, special rules and classification of combinations and chemical compounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial Search Considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Factors to consider before starting a search: claim construction, inventive concept, earlier search results, applicant name searching and whether top-up searching is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes preliminary search and when to perform additional searching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Development of the Search Strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Designing a search strategy: use of Three Person Team (3PT), treatment of independent/dependent/broad claims, reserving the search, and use of controlled language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on selecting areas and fields to search and coordinating team searching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search Area — Patent and Non-Patent Literature
rubrics_metrics.description: Deciding which bodies of literature to search: patent literature (by classification) and relevant non-patent literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes how to find and use classification symbols and guidance on internet and foreign-language searching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conducting the Search — Analysis and Cessation
rubrics_metrics.description: Analysing search results, deciding when the search is complete, and recording reasons for cessation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers useful techniques (piggy-back/forward searching), obtaining full copies, culling documents, categorising citations and ending the search.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording the Search Details
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for documenting fields searched, documents considered relevant, citation categories, dates searched and other search metadata.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes completion of Search Information Statements and annex examples for sequence/chemical searches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formalities and Forms — Formalities Checking
rubrics_metrics.description: Formalities that must be checked at filing and during examination (e.g., credible address for service, required forms and signatures).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists formalities at filing, during examination and approved form requirements including patent request specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal Requirements of the Specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Formatting and content requirements for specifications: title, abstracts, text, pagination, formulas, drawings, graphics, photographs, and sequence listings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes rules for substitute pages, sequence listings and treatment of scandalous matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entitlement (Who may file and be granted a patent)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules on who can file and be granted a patent, statement of entitlement, examples of declarations and treatment of AI inventorship and legal-person examples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes annexed examples and discussion of organisations of uncertain status as legal persons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of Specifications — Purpose and Considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose of construing a specification and factors relevant to construction: the addressee, common general knowledge, and the invention described.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses initial considerations, role of common general knowledge, and how to approach differing aspects claimed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules of Construction for a Specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles such as words given plain meaning, specification read as a whole, purposive construction, dictionary principle, rejection of absurd results, and treating description as a technical document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes treatment of errors, mistakes and omissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim Construction and Claim Types
rubrics_metrics.description: How claims are construed (as legal documents) and types of claims and their special considerations (omnibus, Swiss, product-by-process, parametric, 'for use', 'comprises/includes', reference numerals, relative terms, 'substantially/about').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on presumption against redundancy and treatment of various claim wordings and claim types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination — Relevant Dates, Definitions and Legal Standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Key temporal and definitional matters for examination (priority and filing dates, effect of publication, definitions of 'invention', and the applicable standard of proof such as balance of probabilities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes guidance on applying the balance of probabilities in examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors before Commencing Examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative and procedural considerations to address prior to starting substantive examination: requests for examination, payment of fees, translations, obtaining priority documents, and excess claims fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes dealing with applications in a state of lapse and extension requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification and Claims to Examine — Amendments and Unity
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration of amendments made prior to examination, assessment of unity (single invention), and treatment of provisional specifications and omnibus references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on when to examine amended documents and how to handle lack of unity or complex claim sets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citations: Prior Art Base and Construction of Prior Art
rubrics_metrics.description: What constitutes prior art under the Act (publicly available material, exclusions, grace periods), how to construe cited documents, and the level of disclosure required for a citation to be relevant (enabling disclosure, clear directions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes treatment of single-source documents, combinations of documents, and third party notifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty (Determining Novelty and Whole of Contents)
rubrics_metrics.description: How to determine novelty including whole-of-contents objections, treatment of prior use/secret use/confidential information, selections and chemistry-specific issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annex examples and specific examples for novelty assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive Step (Requirements and Tests)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards and procedures for assessing inventive step (grounds, tests, indicators, identifying relevant information and the person skilled in the art).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes information sources for assessing inventive step, tests to apply, and chemistry-specific issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full Disclosure, Sufficiency, Clarity and Support (s40 considerations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for clear and complete disclosure (s40(2)(a)), support for claims (s40(3)), claims to be clear and succinct, the best method, and specific rules for micro-organisms and sequence deposits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains difference between 'clear and complete disclosure' and 'support' and includes annex examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Eligible Subject Matter (Manner of Manufacture and Usefulness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles for assessing whether subject matter is patentable (manner of manufacture), including exclusions such as discoveries, scientific theories, schemes/plans, printed matter, mathematical algorithms, certain biological subject matter, and other issues (usefulness/utility).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes specific discussions on computer-implemented inventions, methods of testing, nucleic acids, micro-organisms, agriculture, kits/packages, new uses and other borderline categories; annex on history of 'manner of manufacture'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance, Grant and Refusal of Applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Conditions, timing and procedures for accepting, granting, postponing acceptance, extending acceptance periods, revoking acceptance, refusing acceptance and related post-decision processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers consequences of refusal, continued examination, lapsing, withdrawal, and double patenting rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional Applications (Requirements and Time Limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements to claim divisional status, priority entitlement, time limits for filing divisionals, relationship to the parent and examination of divisionals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes procedural outlines and special case management considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments — What Can Be Amended and When
rubrics_metrics.description: Which documents may be amended, who may request amendments (including consent requirements), timing for amendments, requirements to provide reasons, withdrawal of amendments and fees associated with amendments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes allowability rules prior to acceptance, after acceptance, after grant, and special rules for provisional specifications, sequence listings, and amendments during opposition proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments to Correct Clerical Errors or Obvious Mistakes
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions and evidentiary requirements for correcting clerical errors or obvious mistakes in filed documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies what constitutes a clerical error vs an obvious mistake and evidence needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary Search and Opinion (PSO)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for requesting and producing a Preliminary Search and Opinion: search and examination procedure, report requirements and responses to PSO reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains when PSOs are available and how examiners should prepare and respond to them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-Examination and Related Procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Processes to commence and complete re-examination, and possible outcomes including refusal to grant or revocation following re-examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes procedural outlines for initiating re‑examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition Orders and Sensitive Applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Handling applications subject to prohibition orders (e.g., defence-related or associated technology) including their effect and special processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses Chapter 15 applications and technology requiring restricted handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation Patents (System and Examination)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules and procedures specific to innovation patents: formalities, examination, determining innovative step, certification, opposition and expiry/ceasing details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes annexed certification forms and specific procedural outlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: International Searching and PCT Procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural outlines and guidance for PCT international searches, search allocation and classification, unity of invention under PCT, claim interpretation following PCT Guidelines, search strategy and reporting (ISR/ISO), and subjects excluded from search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers Three Person Team (3PT) use, areas of search, non-patent literature, and completion of international search and opinion forms (Box V reasoned statements for novelty/inventive step/industrial applicability).

rubrics_metrics.name: International Examination (IPER/ISO/IPRPII forms and responses)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for international-type examination including first IPE actions, top-up searches, responses to written opinions, completion of ISO/IPEO/IPRPII forms and the content of reasoned statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes PCT third party observations, treatment of formalities, and annex quality checklists and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oppositions, Disputes and Extensions — Role and Powers of the Commissioner
rubrics_metrics.description: Commissioner's powers in hearings and opposition proceedings and procedural summaries for different types of oppositions and disputes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes starting oppositions, filing statements of grounds, evidence periods, finalising oppositions and specific types (section 59/101M/75(1)/104(4)/223(6) etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition Procedure — Evidence and Filing Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules on presentation and admissibility of evidence in opposition proceedings, time limits and consequences of filing evidence late.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers written and oral evidence, physical evidence special considerations and admissibility rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Production of Documents and Summonsing Witnesses
rubrics_metrics.description: Basis and procedure for requesting the Commissioner to exercise powers to summon witnesses or require production of documents, including reasonable expenses, compliance and sanctions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes schedules to requests and grounds for issuing summonses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearings and Decisions — Procedure and Principles of Conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural rules for hearings (setting down, location, who may appear, hours, fees), hearings conduct (adjournments, confidential material, consultation) and principles of decision-making including lawfulness, fairness, rationality, openness, diligence, efficiency, courtesy and integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also addresses natural justice, bias, written decisions, time for issuing decisions, publication and rectification of errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Costs — Principles and Scales
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles for awarding costs in proceedings, scale of costs, taxation and exemplary situations for awarding costs or security for costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on calculation, variation and awarding processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Register of Patents — Recording Particulars and Effects
rubrics_metrics.description: What the Register is, procedures for recording new particulars, recording change of ownership (assignment, name change, bankruptcy, death), security interests, licences, court orders and the effect of registration or non-registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes rectification procedures, types of errors that can be rectified and discretionary considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions of Time and Restoration of Priority (Section 223 and Reg 5.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Grounds, procedures and discretionary considerations for extensions of time (section 223 subsections, Regulation 5.9), filing requests, common deficiencies and restoration of priority under the PCT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes annex file note examples and guidance on 'despite due care' provision, advertising extensions and handling fee/payment/timeline consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions of Term for Pharmaceutical Substances (Section 70)
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria and procedural steps for applying for and processing extensions of patent term relating to pharmaceutical substances including definitions (pharmaceutical substance, first regulatory approval date) and calculations of extension length.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes required documentation, timing, processing steps and opposition handling for extensions of term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals, Judicial Review and Recourse
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeal routes (Federal Court, Administrative Review Tribunal, ADJR), procedures for appeals and related actions involving the Commissioner, including section 105 amendments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on interplay with court proceedings and limits on office actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computerised Decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Power to make computerised decisions, substituting and existing computerised decisions and relevant procedural limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers how automated decision-making may be used and substituted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Superseded Legislation and Practice — Historical Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Summary and guidance on how to treat applications/examinations under superseded legislation and prior practice, and differences in law and practice over time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes discussion of legacy approaches to examination, novelty and inventive step under former provisions, and transitional treatment of amendments.
